newsitem.title: INDIA: Congress says India government safe for the moment.
newsitem.headline: Congress says India government safe for the moment.

text.p: India's Congress party said on Wednesday that it will not immediately move to topple the United Front government it has reluctantly supported for nine months.

"It won't fall this year," Congress spokesman Vithal Gadgil told Reuters when asked if Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government might fall during the three-month long budget session of parliament which opens on Thursday. "It will at least survive the budget session."

Deve Gowda has fewer than 200 deputies in the 545-member lower house of parliament. The Congress, which controls some 140 deputies, said over the weekend its support for the government was no longer unconditional.

The Congress Working Committee, the party's main policy-making body, issued a statement accusing the United Front minority coalition of failing to work with it to fight against the Hindu nationalist opposition.

India's main opposition rightwing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party has said it is considering moving a no-confidence motion against Deve Gowda during the budget session. Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is scheduled to unveil the nation's budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) on February 28.
